domains.name: Guest stays
domains.summary: Looking after guests from their booking to their check-out.

domains.name: Property
domains.summary: Keeping the hotel ready for guests.
domains.body: Maintenance belongs here too, once the software takes on that job.

features.name: Reservations
features.summary: Taking bookings and handling changes to them, before the guest arrives.

features.name: Front desk
features.summary: Welcoming guests when they arrive and settling up when they leave.

features.name: Housekeeping
features.summary: Keeping rooms ready for the next guest.

personas.name: Maria, front desk clerk
personas.summary: Runs the front desk: takes bookings, and checks guests in and out.
personas.body:
## Needs

- To tell a guest at once whether a room is free for their dates, and hold it
  for them, without ever giving the same room to two guests.
- To check guests in and out quickly, so nobody waits at the desk.
- To know which rooms are ready before a guest arrives, without phoning
  housekeeping.

## Knows

Every room in the hotel, the regulars, and the cancellation policy by heart.
Comfortable with a computer, but has learned the system on the job, not from a
manual.

## Context

At the desk all shift, on a shared desktop, with a guest or the phone waiting
most of the time. Interrupted constantly, so anything they start may be
finished minutes later.

## Expects

The paper diary's view of the hotel: rooms down the side, nights across the
top. Talks about stays, rooms and arrivals, not reservations or inventory.

## Cares about

Never having to tell a guest standing in front of them that their room was
given away. They'll go back to the paper diary the first time the app gets
that wrong.

personas.name: Ana, housekeeper
personas.summary: Cleans and readies the rooms between guests.
personas.body:
## Needs

- To know which rooms to clean first, so arriving guests don't wait for a
  room.
- To tell the front desk a room is ready without walking back down to say so.

## Knows

The building, floor by floor, and how long each kind of room takes. Uses a
phone every day, but rarely for work.

## Context

On their feet, moving from room to room with a trolley, a phone in their pocket.
Gloves on much of the time, so anything they do has to take a tap or two.

## Expects

A list of rooms, in the order they'll do them. Talks about rooms being clean,
dirty or ready.

## Cares about

Not being rushed by the front desk for a room they didn't know was urgent.

personas.name: David, hotel manager
personas.summary: Runs the hotel, and answers for its takings to the owners.
personas.body:
## Needs

- To set what each room costs, night by night, so busy dates earn more.

## Knows

The local market and the hotel's busy seasons. Reads a spreadsheet well, and
expects software to do the arithmetic for them.

## Context

At a desk in the back office, a few times a week, in between everything else
running a hotel brings.

## Expects

A calendar of rates, like the one they keep in a spreadsheet today.

## Cares about

Rates they can change in a minute when a big event is announced, and being sure
the front desk is quoting them.

capabilities.name: Room booking
capabilities.summary: Clerks book a free room for a guest's stay.
capabilities.body:
## Covers

- Clerks see which rooms are free for a stay.
- Clerks move a booking to new dates.

## Success

- The front desk stops keeping the paper diary alongside the app.

capabilities.name: Cancellations
capabilities.summary: Clerks cancel a booking when a guest's plans change, and the guest is refunded what the cancellation policy allows.
capabilities.body:
## Covers

- Clerks tell a guest what they'd be refunded if they cancelled now.

## Open decisions

- **No-shows:** is a guest who never arrives treated as a late cancellation, or
  charged for the whole stay?

capabilities.name: Check-in
capabilities.summary: Clerks check guests in when they arrive and give them their room.
capabilities.body:
## Covers

- Clerks see today's arrivals.
- Clerks move a guest to another room for the rest of their stay.

## Success

- A guest with a booking is checked in within two minutes of reaching the desk.

capabilities.name: Check-out
capabilities.summary: Clerks check guests out on their departure day and take payment for anything still owed.
capabilities.body:
## Covers

- Clerks see today's departures.

## Success

- The front desk closes the day with every departure settled.

capabilities.name: Cleaning schedule
capabilities.summary: Housekeepers see which rooms to clean today, with early arrivals first.
capabilities.body:
## Learning

- Is ordering by arrival time enough, or do housekeepers plan by floor?

capabilities.name: Group bookings
capabilities.summary: Clerks hold several rooms at once for a group travelling together, under one name.
capabilities.body:
## Learning

- Do groups want one booking with many rooms, or many bookings linked
  together?

capabilities.name: Rate calendar
capabilities.summary: Managers set each room type's nightly rate, date by date.
capabilities.body:
## Learning

- Do rates change often enough to need a calendar, or is a rate per season
  enough?

capabilities.name: Room status
capabilities.summary: Housekeepers mark rooms clean or dirty, so the front desk knows which are ready.
capabilities.body:
## Covers

- Clerks see which rooms are ready for arriving guests.

## Learning

- Will housekeepers update a room's status as they go, or at the end of their
  round?

rules.name: A room can't be double-booked
rules.summary: Two bookings for the same room can't share a night. A cancelled booking no longer holds its nights.

rules.name: A stay is at least one night
rules.summary: A booking's check-out date is after its check-in date.

verifiedBy.test: parseStay > rejects a stay that ends the day it starts

rules.name: A stay can start on the day another ends
rules.summary: A room can be booked from the day an earlier booking checks out, because the two stays don't share a night.
rules.body:
## Why

Guests check out by 11:00 and check in from 15:00, which leaves time to clean
the room.

rules.name: Cancelling 48 hours ahead is free
rules.summary: A booking cancelled at least 48 hours before check-in is refunded in full.

rules.name: A late cancellation costs the first night
rules.summary: A booking cancelled less than 48 hours before check-in is refunded everything except the first night.
rules.body:
## Why

The room usually can't be rebooked at such short notice.

concepts.name: Booking
concepts.summary: A guest's hold on one room for a stay, from a check-in date to a check-out date.
concepts.body:
## Details

A booking is for one [room](room.md). Its nights run from the check-in date up
to, but not including, the check-out date.

## Lifecycle

Confirmed → Checked in → Checked out

A confirmed booking can instead be Cancelled, any time before check-in.

concepts.name: Room
concepts.summary: A room guests can stay in, known by its number.
concepts.body:
## Details

Each room has a type, such as double or twin, which sets its rate. A room is
[booked](booking.md) a night at a time.

gaps.text: When every room is taken there's no waitlist. Clerks note the guest's details outside the app and call them if a room frees up.
A booking holds one room, so a family that needs two rooms makes two bookings.
The late-cancellation fee isn't charged yet, so every cancellation is refunded in full.

problems.subject: rule:booking/same-day-turnover
problems.message: Room booking is Beta, which needs edge-case rules passing, but this rule has no verifying test.
